subject.title: [Bug]: tools.elevated.allowFrom.slack silently blocked by commandAuthorized gate — no documented fallback for Slack

question: Should Slack room/group `/elevated` text commands be allowed to reach elevated permission checks when the sender matches `tools.elevated.allowFrom.slack` but not `channels.slack.allowFrom` or `channels.slack.channels.<id>.users`?
rationale: The source-reproducible failure is real, but the repair changes which Slack messages can cross the command gate before elevated security checks run, so maintainer intent is needed before automation widens the boundary.

options.title: Add a narrow elevated exception
options.body: Authorize only `/elevated` text directives from the Slack elevated allowlist, then let existing elevated permission checks accept or deny the sender with a visible response.

options.title: Keep strict command auth
options.body: Require Slack command authorization separately and document the prerequisite plus a visible denial path instead of letting elevated allowlists affect command ingress.

options.title: Unify channel fallback hooks
options.body: Register channel-level elevated fallback adapters for Slack and Discord together, accepting the broader cross-channel semantics work before merge.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow elevated exception
recommendation.body: Authorize only `/elevated` text directives from the Slack elevated allowlist, then let existing elevated permission checks accept or deny the sender with a visible response.

likelyOwner.reason: The open choice is the shared security/command-gating boundary introduced and most often maintained by this owner history.
